question: If two strangers get into a physical fight at a busy local market, what type of violence is this considered?

options.A: Intimate partner violence
options.B: Community violence
options.C: Collective violence
options.D: Self-directed violence

explanation: Well done! When violence happens outside the home between people who are unrelated and often don't know each other, we call it community violence. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T14#GNS313_U3_T14_h2)

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Symptoms, Body, Analysis, Response
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Safety, Behavior, Action, Review
options.D: Staff, Bedside, Assessment, Report

explanation: SBAR provides a standardized, concise framework for sharing critical patient updates among health professionals. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h7)

question: What is the main goal of taking a dietary supplement?

options.A: To completely replace regular hospital meals
options.B: To add extra nutrients to a person's diet
options.C: To cure chronic infectious diseases overnight
options.D: To serve as the main source of daily calories

explanation: Supplements are simply meant to top up the nutrients you might be missing from your regular meals. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h1)

question: Why must nurses always ask patients if they are taking traditional or herbal remedies along with prescribed drugs?

options.A: To calculate the patient's daily fluid intake and output accurately
options.B: To prevent dangerous herb-drug interactions that could harm the patient
options.C: To prove that orthodox medicine is superior to cultural treatments
options.D: To report traditional healers to the local pharmaceutical board

explanation: Herbs are powerful! Mixing them with hospital medications can cause bad reactions or stop the prescribed drug from working. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why do many patients hide their use of traditional home remedies from doctors and nurses?

options.A: Herbal remedies leave no physical trace in the body
options.B: Fear of being scolded or dismissed by healthcare providers
options.C: They believe nurses already monitor everything they ingest
options.D: Because hospital rules forbid talking about home treatments

explanation: Exactly. Patients often stay quiet because they worry healthcare workers will judge or mock their cultural healing practices. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h4)

question: How do the ovaries communicate back to the brain about their hormone levels?

options.A: By altering the physical size of the pituitary gland
options.B: By sending electrical impulses down the spinal cord
options.C: By sending estrogen and progesterone through the blood
options.D: By releasing white blood cells into lymphatic channels

explanation: Ovarian hormones travel through the bloodstream to send feedback signals back to the brain (the hypothalamus and pituitary gland). Simple and amazing how the body works! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h3)

question: A nurse assesses a wound and notes it as 'mild, moderate, or severe'. What scale of measurement is this?

options.A: Ratio scale
options.B: Nominal scale
options.C: Interval scale
options.D: Ordinal scale

explanation: Because the wound grades follow a clear rank order from best to worst, we call this an ordinal scale. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T1#GNS217_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why is a pressure bandage placed on the arm right after an implant procedure?

options.A: To keep the arm completely paralyzed for two weeks
options.B: To prevent the hormone from leaking into the air
options.C: To push the implant deep down into the bone marrow
options.D: To minimize bruising and swelling at the site

explanation: The pressure bandage acts as a gentle hug for the insertion site during the first 24 hours, keeping swelling and bruising down to a minimum. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h8)

question: Why do nurses flush an intermittent IV line with normal saline right after giving a medication?

options.A: To clear remaining drug residue and prevent line clotting
options.B: To dilute any air bubbles that entered during the injection
options.C: To numb the vein so the patient feels less soreness
options.D: To cool down the internal walls of the plastic tubing

explanation: Well done! Flushing pushes any leftover medication completely through the catheter, keeping the line clear and preventing clots. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T6#GNS311_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the correct management advice for a mother who develops mastitis in one breast?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent the infection from spreading
options.B: Continue breastfeeding frequently to keep the milk draining out
options.C: Apply ice packs to freeze the infected milk inside the milk ducts
options.D: Stop feeding from the affected side completely until the pain stops

explanation: Frequent milk removal is vital in treating mastitis because letting milk pool in the breast makes the infection worse. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: Which type of drink should patients avoid right after a tonsillectomy so you can easily spot if they are bleeding?

options.A: Clear water
options.B: Apple juice
options.C: Plain milk
options.D: Red-colored fluids

explanation: You got it! We avoid red drinks because if the patient vomits or spits up, the red color looks just like fresh blood and can easily cause a false alarm (or hide real bleeding). [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h6)

question: How do Mastomys rats spread the Lassa virus around?

options.A: By biting humans aggressively during daylight hours
options.B: By carrying ticks that drop onto human skin
options.C: By shedding the virus in their urine, faeces, and saliva
options.D: Through respiratory droplets when they sneeze or cough

explanation: Even though the rats don't look sick, their droppings and urine constantly contaminate food items and household surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h2)

question: A mother brings her toddler to a primary health care clinic with watery diarrhea and sunken eyes. According to standing orders for gastroenteritis, what is the priority intervention?

options.A: Wait for a visiting medical consultant to arrive next week before acting
options.B: Refer the child straight to a tertiary teaching hospital for surgery
options.C: Assess hydration status and initiate rehydration therapy immediately
options.D: Prescribe strong sleeping pills to keep the child quiet during the day

explanation: Primary care standing orders for gastroenteritis prioritize checking hydration and starting oral rehydration or fluids to prevent shock. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h5)

question: When a patient resists your care during a home visit, what does it most likely mean?

options.A: Proof that the patient has fully recovered from illness
options.B: Fear and a desire to retain personal control and independence
options.C: A deliberate plot to get the nurse fired from the agency
options.D: A lack of respect for human rights laws in medicine

explanation: Correct! Resistance is often just a defense mechanism. Patients are usually scared of losing their independence and are trying to hold onto control of their lives. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h6)

question: According to child protection laws, how should young offenders be housed while in detention?

options.A: Placed in the same cells as hardened adult criminals for deterrence
options.B: Released immediately without any form of supervision or tracking
options.C: Separated entirely from adult inmates in specialized facilities
options.D: Kept in solitary confinement within maximum security prisons

explanation: You've got this! To keep young ones safe from abuse and bad influences, the law requires that they be kept completely away from adult criminals. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why must you use a filter needle when drawing medication out of a glass ampoule?

options.A: To catch microscopic glass fragments
options.B: To prevent the plunger from sticking
options.C: To filter out air bubbles in the liquid
options.D: To neutralize chemical impurities

explanation: Snap! Snapping open that glass top creates tiny, invisible glass shards. A filter needle acts like a tiny shield, catching those shards so they never make it into the syringe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h4)

question: A patient suddenly falls asleep during the day and feels weak when feeling strong emotions. What condition is this?

options.A: Insomnia
options.B: Narcolepsy
options.C: Somnambulism
options.D: Sleep apnea

explanation: Narcolepsy causes sudden sleep attacks during the day. Strong emotions can sometimes trigger sudden muscle weakness called cataplexy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h8)

question: How does good family nutrition directly help a patient managing HIV?

options.A: It cures any underlying opportunistic infections present
options.B: It replaces the need for daily medication intake
options.C: It guarantees an immediate increase in white blood cells
options.D: It strengthens immunity and helps process medications

explanation: Well done! Nutritious meals support overall body strength and help the system tolerate drug regimens successfully. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h5)

question: In the FAST stroke assessment tool, what does the letter 'A' stand for?

options.A: Arm weakness
options.B: Acute anxiety
options.C: Ataxia severity
options.D: Airway blockage

explanation: Correct! 'A' stands for arm weakness. We check if one arm drifts downward when the patient tries to hold both arms up. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why does the infection control team monitor how well hospital surfaces are cleaned?

options.A: To make sure the hospital floors always shine brightly for visiting inspectors
options.B: Because many harmful pathogens can survive on dry hospital surfaces for long periods
options.C: To keep the housekeeping department busy between their regular meal breaks
options.D: Because cleaning chemicals are expensive and must be rationed carefully

explanation: Correct! Germs can hide out on bedrails, trays, and tables for ages if we don't clean them properly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h7)

question: What happens to the tiny coronary blood vessels when local waste products like adenosine pile up?

options.A: They constrict to stop bleeding.
options.B: They harden into rigid fibrous tubes.
options.C: They collapse from high pressure.
options.D: They dilate to increase blood flow.

explanation: Well done! Metabolic waste acts like a chemical green light, telling the blood vessels to relax and open wide so more oxygen can reach hardworking tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is another common name for the normal bacteria and microbes living on and inside the human body?

options.A: Human microbiota
options.B: Somatic organisms
options.C: Pathogenic colonies
options.D: Acellular particles

explanation: You've got this! 'Human microbiota' is just the scientific term for the friendly community of microbes that call our bodies home. Every healthy person has them! [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h1)

question: A client with gout is prescribed a loop diuretic for heart failure. What is the main risk?

options.A: It prevents oral gout medications from ever working again
options.B: It causes immediate permanent stiffness in the large toe joints
options.C: It can raise blood uric acid levels and precipitate an acute gout attack
options.D: It will dissolve joint cartilage and accelerate osteoarthritis

explanation: Loop diuretics make it harder for the kidneys to clear out uric acid. Higher uric acid in the blood means a much higher chance of a painful flare! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which of these is a great example of working with another sector to stop the spread of infections like cholera?

options.A: Hospital pharmacists reviewing drug expiration dates in the dispensary
options.B: Doctors prescribing antibiotics in a private clinic setting
options.C: A head nurse holding a closed meeting with junior nursing students
options.D: Working with public works to ensure clean water supply to prevent cholera

explanation: Spot on! Teaming up with public works to fix water infrastructure stops waterborne diseases right at the source. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h3)

question: What is the most important thing for a nurse to check right after giving a nebulizer treatment with a beta-agonist?

options.A: Checking the patient for signs of severe weight gain
options.B: Reassessing lung sounds and respiratory effort
options.C: Offering the patient a heavy, high-sodium meal
options.D: Inspecting the skin for signs of bruising or rashes

explanation: Always close the loop! Listening to the patient's lungs afterward lets you know right away if the medication did its job and made breathing easier. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h4)

question: What does 'external validity' deal with?

options.A: How fast data goes into the hospital computer
options.B: How well patients understand their consent forms
options.C: Whether the study results can apply to other patients in the real world
options.D: How accurate the thermometers are in the laboratory

explanation: External validity asks: 'If this worked in a tiny research lab, will it also work for our patients out here on the busy hospital wards?' [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h3)

question: When you support the joint above and below the moving area during exercise, what are you doing?

options.A: To stop blood flow completely to the lower arm.
options.B: To force the joint to bend past its normal breaking point.
options.C: To replace the patient's muscle power with nurse strength.
options.D: To provide stability and protect the limb during movement.

explanation: Supporting the limbs properly keeps the movement steady and shields the surrounding tissues from unnecessary strain. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h5)

question: A patient hears voices when no one is around. What do we call this?

options.A: Delusion
options.B: Flight of ideas
options.C: Hallucination
options.D: Concrete thinking

explanation: Great job! Hearing things that aren't actually there is an auditory hallucination. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T3#GNS324_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask a fainting patient about visual changes before the event?

options.A: It indicates that permanent blindness is about to occur.
options.B: It helps confirm a vasovagal prodrome rather than sudden cardiac arrest.
options.C: It proves the patient has an underlying eye disease.
options.D: It shows that the patient's blood sugar was extremely high.

explanation: Cardiac syncope usually strikes instantly without warning, whereas vasovagal syncope gives prodromal visual and physical signs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why does a sudden dip in blood sugar so quickly lead to confusion and fainting?

options.A: Low sugar causes the brain cells to instantly swell with extra fluid
options.B: The liver stops sending oxygen to the head during sugar crashes
options.C: Nerves stop producing insulin when blood sugar drops below normal
options.D: The brain relies entirely on a continuous supply of circulating glucose

explanation: Unlike other tissues, your brain cells don't store fuel. When blood glucose takes a dive, the brain feels it instantly! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h3)

question: Why do children need especially fast nursing action during emergencies compared to adults?

options.A: Children are always more cooperative with nursing staff than adults
options.B: Children never experience true medical emergencies
options.C: Pediatric equipment is much harder to find in a standard hospital
options.D: Children have smaller physical reserves and deteriorate much faster

explanation: Because children have lower physical reserves, a minor illness or breathing problem can quickly turn serious if we don't catch it early. You're building great clinical intuition! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h4)

question: A village starts the year with no cholera, but 10 people fall sick by March. What do these 10 new cases represent?

options.A: The recovery rate of the infected population
options.B: The prevalence of cholera in the village
options.C: The mortality rate of the disease outbreak
options.D: The incidence of cholera for that period

explanation: Because these 10 folks developed the illness during that time window, they are the brand-new cases—making it the incidence! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h2)

question: What is the main reason for using strict aseptic technique during an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To keep the doctor's hands clean during the procedure
options.B: To make the injection completely painless for the patient
options.C: To prevent introducing bacteria that cause septic arthritis
options.D: To ensure the medication absorbs faster into the bloodstream

explanation: Strict sterility protects the joint capsule from dangerous bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why is proper patient allocation so important during staffing?

options.A: It ensures everyone works the exact same night shifts
options.B: It eliminates the need for shift handovers
options.C: It matches staff skills and experience with patient care needs
options.D: It guarantees hospital operating costs stay at zero

explanation: Matching the right nurse to the right patient keeps everyone safe and prevents junior nurses from feeling overwhelmed. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which tool is commonly used to check distant vision during routine school health checks?

options.A: Peak flow meter
options.B: Otoscope
options.C: Sphygmomanometer
options.D: Snellen chart

explanation: You got it! The Snellen chart with rows of letters is the classic tool for checking how well school children can see from a distance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women at a much higher risk of getting severe malaria?

options.A: They spend more time outdoors during peak mosquito biting hours
options.B: They experience natural immunological changes that lower resistance to the parasite
options.C: They are completely allergic to standard antimalarial medications
options.D: Their bodies produce extra iron that feeds the malaria parasite directly

explanation: Correct! Pregnancy naturally shifts the immune system to protect the baby, which unfortunately makes it easier for the malaria parasite to take hold. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T4#GNS313_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is skin turgor checked over the clavicle or forearm during a physical assessment?

options.A: To evaluate the patient's overall hydration status
options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure in the upper body
options.C: To check for localized muscle weakness under the skin
options.D: To determine if the patient has a superficial fungal infection

explanation: Skin turgor reflects how quickly the skin returns to its normal flat position, which helps nurses estimate body fluid volume and hydration. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is the main job of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) in the lab?

options.A: To grow fastidious bacteria on solid blood agar plates
options.B: To make many copies of tiny amounts of microbial DNA so they are easy to spot
options.C: To physically stain cell walls purple under a light microscope
options.D: To measure the patient's antibody response to a viral infection

explanation: Spot on! PCR is like a genetic photocopier that makes millions of copies of a germ's DNA so we can find even tiny traces. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h7)

question: Where is it completely inappropriate to discuss confidential patient handover details?

options.A: At the patient's bedside with privacy curtains drawn
options.B: In a public hospital cafeteria or open hallway
options.C: During a structured team conference meeting
options.D: Inside a private, closed nursing station room

explanation: Public spots let unauthorized people overhear private medical information, which breaks patient confidentiality. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the popular local name for the skin boils caused by tumbu fly larvae in West Africa?

options.A: Guinea worm blister
options.B: Ground itch
options.C: Mango fly boil or 'tsoro'
options.D: Jigger foot

explanation: Tumbu fly larvae burrow under the skin to form raised, boil-like sores that locals commonly call mango fly boils or 'tsoro'. Excellent local clinical context! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is Asherman syndrome?

options.A: The complete absence of the ovaries since birth
options.B: An abnormal widening of the cervical canal due to infection
options.C: The formation of scar tissue inside the uterine cavity
options.D: A benign growth of muscle tissue on the outer wall of the uterus

explanation: Correct! Asherman syndrome happens when scar tissue forms inside the womb—often after past surgeries or procedures—causing the walls to stick together. Learning everyday clinical terms like this makes you a stronger nurse! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h4)

question: Which clinical finding during a routine physical checkup might first alert a nurse to the presence of past FGM?

options.A: Enlarged thyroid gland in the neck
options.B: Spontaneous bruising on the upper extremities
options.C: Unexplained scarring and altered anatomy of the external genitalia
options.D: Asymmetrical deep tendon reflexes in the lower limbs

explanation: Visual inspection during relevant examinations often reveals missing structures or dense scar tissue characteristic of previous mutilation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: What major global health target was famously set by the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Eradication of all infectious diseases by 1985
options.B: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.C: Privatization of all national health sectors
options.D: Free tertiary hospital care for every global citizen

explanation: Alma-Ata made history by rallying the world around the bold dream of 'Health for All by the Year 2000' through primary care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of antiemetic medications?

options.A: Lowering high blood glucose levels in diabetes
options.B: Preventing or relieving nausea and vomiting
options.C: Stimulating regular bowel movements
options.D: Reducing excess stomach acid production

explanation: Antiemetics target the vomiting center in the brain or gut to help settle an upset stomach and stop vomiting. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why does high-intensity exercise without enough oxygen lead to muscle fatigue?

options.A: The motor neurons stop producing acetylcholine forever
options.B: Lactic acid builds up and energy supplies run low
options.C: The bones dissolve inside the connective tissue wrappings
options.D: Muscle fibers permanently lose all of their calcium

explanation: Anaerobic metabolism produces lactic acid and uses up energy stores quickly, contributing to cellular fatigue and soreness. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which detail is NOT required when documenting a new peripheral IV insertion?

options.A: The catheter gauge and anatomical location
options.B: The brand name of the soap used for handwashing
options.C: The patient's response and tolerance to the procedure
options.D: The date and exact time of the insertion

explanation: Standard hand hygiene is assumed; charting focuses on the specific procedure details like size, location, time, and patient response. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h10)

question: What does 'self-financing' mean for a DRF scheme?

options.A: It generates enough revenue from sales to buy replacement stock
options.B: It borrows money from private banks whenever stocks get low
options.C: It relies entirely on yearly donations from foreign countries
options.D: It receives unlimited free drugs from the central ministry

explanation: Great job! Self-financing just means the fund keeps itself alive through patient payments instead of waiting for outside help. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T8#GNS223_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why is a luminal medication also prescribed along with tissue-active drugs?

options.A: To replace lost electrolytes and boost red blood cell production
options.B: To permanently numb the lining of the stomach against acid
options.C: To speed up the healing of skin lesions on the abdomen
options.D: To clear remaining cysts from the bowel lumen and prevent relapse

explanation: Exactly! While one drug clears the tissues, the luminal agent mops up any cysts left in the gut so the infection doesn't bounce back. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h5)

question: Why would a dietitian need to check laboratory test results during a patient assessment?

options.A: To spot hidden signs of malnutrition or metabolic imbalance
options.B: To calculate the exact cost of hospital food supplies
options.C: To diagnose infectious diseases independent of a doctor
options.D: To determine when a patient is ready for physical therapy

explanation: You got it! Lab values like albumin and blood glucose give clear, objective proof of how well a patient's body is handling nutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h3)

question: Why are anti-diarrhea drugs sometimes avoided when a patient has an infection causing their diarrhea?

options.A: Diarrhea helps the kidneys filter extra salt from the blood
options.B: Antibiotics are the only approved treatment for any diarrhea
options.C: These medications always cause permanent bowel paralysis instantly
options.D: Stopping stool too fast can trap harmful bacteria inside the body

explanation: Makes sense, right? Diarrhea is actually the body's way of flushing out bad germs. Shutting it down too quickly can trap those toxins inside. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary function of GABA in the central nervous system?

options.A: To trigger happy memories in the frontal lobe
options.B: To stimulate muscle movement in the arms and legs
options.C: To calm nervous system activity and reduce anxiety
options.D: To increase blood pressure during a physical threat

explanation: GABA is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter, meaning it slows down brain activity to keep anxiety levels manageable. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a major benefit of buying local Nigerian food staples during harvest season?

options.A: They are always imported from abroad
options.B: They have longer artificial shelf lives
options.C: They require no washing or cooking
options.D: They are cheaper and more nutritious

explanation: In-season local foods are harvested at peak ripeness, offering better nutrients at lower market prices due to high supply. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h7)

question: Why is it so important to encourage a patient to drink lots of fluids after a bone scan?

options.A: To prevent severe dehydration caused by the strong magnetic fields
options.B: To replace the fluid lost during the mandatory fasting period before the test
options.C: To activate the chemical tracer so it can take clearer pictures of the spine
options.D: To help flush the remaining radioactive tracer out of the body through urine

explanation: Drinking plenty of water helps the kidneys wash out any leftover radioactive tracer quickly, lowering radiation exposure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is GNP an important concept for nurses to understand?

options.A: It reflects national wealth which influences funding available for health services
options.B: It determines the price of essential pharmaceutical drugs in local pharmacies
options.C: It measures the exact recovery rate of patients admitted to emergency wards
options.D: It dictates the individual salaries of clinical nurses in public hospitals

explanation: When a country's economy does well (high GNP), the government has more money to build better hospitals and support public health. Everything is connected! [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h1)

question: How many signal functions must a health facility perform to be called a BEmOC center?

options.A: Three signal functions
options.B: Ten signal functions
options.C: Twelve signal functions
options.D: Seven signal functions

explanation: To be officially recognized as a Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC) center, a facility must be able to handle all seven specific medical interventions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h2)

question: Why might an MRI or ultrasound be ordered for a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: To check for active urinary tract infections
options.B: To test the patient's liver enzymes and kidney function
options.C: To evaluate the condition of the sphincter muscles and surrounding deep tissues
options.D: To measure the patient's daily fluid intake and output

explanation: Advanced imaging helps surgeons see the exact path of the fistula and check if the anal sphincter muscles are also injured. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why do incubatory carriers give nurses headaches when trying to stop the spread of disease?

options.A: They spread pathogens before anyone realizes they are sick
options.B: They only transmit infections through contaminated drinking water
options.C: They carry drug-resistant bacteria that resist all antibiotics
options.D: They refuse to take their prescribed medications in the ward

explanation: Since they look and feel healthy right now, nobody suspects they are passing germs around until symptoms finally show up later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h2)

question: What is the primary medical treatment for endocrine hyposecretion?

options.A: High-dose antibiotic therapy
options.B: Hormone replacement therapy
options.C: Strict long-term fluid restriction
options.D: Surgical removal of the gland

explanation: Simple logic: if the body isn't making enough of a vital hormone, we replace it with medication! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the go-to treatment for primary hyperparathyroidism caused by a single adenoma?

options.A: Surgical removal of the affected gland
options.B: Strict dietary restriction of all dairy products
options.C: Complete removal of the entire thyroid gland
options.D: Long-term high-dose oral calcitonin therapy

explanation: Taking out the troublesome adenoma through surgery (parathyroidectomy) is the quickest way to cure primary hyperparathyroidism. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h8)

question: What does the important humanitarian principle of 'non-refoulement' mean?

options.A: Automatic granting of permanent citizenship in the host nation
options.B: The legal right to free higher education in the host country
options.C: Protection from being forced to return to a dangerous country

explanation: Easy peasy! Cumulative incidence is often called incidence proportion because it shows the proportion of the group that gets sick over time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h4)

question: Where should you file an incident report after a medication mishap?

options.A: In the hospital's internal quality improvement system
options.B: In the public national medical registry
options.C: In the patient's permanent clinical medical record
options.D: In the personal nursing license file

explanation: Correct! Incident reports go into the hospital's internal quality system to help us learn and improve—they don't go into the patient's official clinical chart. [learn more](GST319_U5_T1#GST319_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which scenario is an example of acquiring passive immunity?

options.A: An adolescent developing long-term immunity after a live vaccine
options.B: A healthy adult receiving a routine tetanus booster shot
options.C: An infant receiving protective antibodies through breast milk
options.D: A child recovering completely from a natural chickenpox infection

explanation: Passive immunity involves receiving ready-made antibodies from an external source rather than making them yourself. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h5)

question: Which type of budget takes care of daily running costs like medical supplies and generator fuel?

options.A: Emergency surplus budget
options.B: Capital budget
options.C: Operational budget
options.D: Personal investment budget

explanation: The operational budget keeps the lights on and the supplies stocked for everyday patient care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h7)

question: A lab report describes tissue with disordered growth and cells of varying shapes and sizes. Which term describes this?

options.A: Metaplasia
options.B: Dysplasia
options.C: Hyperplasia
options.D: Atrophy

explanation: Well done! Dysplasia means disordered growth where cells lose their normal shape and organization—often an early warning sign that nurses watch closely. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of health care waste management?

options.A: To prevent infection and environmental harm
options.B: To create extra work for nursing staff
options.C: To reduce hospital running costs
options.D: To clear up floor space in wards

explanation: Managing medical waste safely stops the spread of disease and protects both hospital workers and the outside community from dangerous materials. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common risk factor for stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Obesity and excess body weight
options.B: Menopause and decreased estrogen levels
options.C: Frequent high-fluid intake throughout the day
options.D: Vaginal childbirth and multiple pregnancies

explanation: Drinking plenty of water is healthy! The real risk factors involve things that weaken pelvic support, like childbirth, hormonal shifts, or heavy pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: Why should hospitals offer counseling and support to nurses involved in errors?

options.A: To help them process their trauma and prevent severe burnout
options.B: To prevent them from talking to hospital management ever again
options.C: To ensure they can be easily monitored for future illegal activities
options.D: To replace their clinical training with psychological theory

explanation: Clinical errors take a heavy emotional toll. Providing support helps nurses heal and protects them from burning out. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h7)

question: What nursing action should be completed just before the procedure starts?

options.A: Place the patient flat on their back with pillows
options.B: Shave the entire back from shoulders to hips
options.C: Administer a strong sleeping pill by mouth
options.D: Ask the patient to empty their urinary bladder

explanation: Correct! An empty bladder keeps the patient comfortable while they stay curled up in a tight position during the test. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to health behavior change in primary care?

options.A: High rates of illiteracy among the target audience
options.B: Extreme poverty and lack of basic financial resources
options.C: Deep-seated cultural norms and traditional beliefs
options.D: Guaranteed financial wealth for every household

explanation: Poverty, illiteracy, and strong cultural traditions can make health changes tough, but having guaranteed wealth certainly wouldn't be a barrier! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h8)

question: Which of these common infections spreads mainly through direct skin-to-skin touch?

options.A: Scabies
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Tuberculosis
options.D: Tetanus

explanation: Scabies is caused by tiny mites that love to crawl from one person's skin straight onto another during close contact. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way for a community to prevent parasitic diseases?

options.A: Promoting open defecation near residential water sources
options.B: Advocating for safe sewage disposal infrastructure
options.C: Distributing protective footwear in farming communities
options.D: Encouraging regular handwashing with soap and clean water

explanation: Spot on! Open defecation near water supplies spreads disease rather than stopping it. Handwashing, good sewage systems, and shoes are brilliant preventative steps. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h6)

question: What does 'U=U' (Undetectable = Untransmittable) mean for an HIV-positive person?

options.A: They are completely cured and no longer carry the virus in their body.
options.B: Their blood tests will no longer show any positive antibody results.
options.C: They cannot sexually transmit the virus if their viral load remains suppressed.
options.D: They can safely stop taking their daily medication without losing immune health.

explanation: When ART keeps the viral load undetectable, the virus cannot be passed on sexually. Amazing science! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common risk of healthcare outsourcing?

options.A: Risk of compromised care quality due to aggressive cost-cutting
options.B: Guaranteed universal access to free healthcare for all citizens
options.C: Difficulty in monitoring complex vendor performance contracts
options.D: Potential loss of direct control over daily hospital operations

explanation: Outsourcing and private partnerships actually tend to threaten free universal access, rather than guarantee it, because private operators need to make money. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is relying only on the average (mean) value of patient data sometimes tricky?

options.A: It is always mathematically incorrect to use averages in healthcare research
options.B: It completely hides the most common value in the distribution
options.C: It changes based on the total number of patients in the study
options.D: It does not show how spread out or inconsistent the individual readings are

explanation: Averages can hide the whole story! Two wards might have the same average temperature, but one ward has everyone very stable while the other has wild highs and lows. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T5#GNS217_U4_T5_h1)

question: A patient develops sudden confusion and a high fever two days after surgery. What is a key trap the nurse must avoid?

options.A: Reporting the temperature change immediately to the attending surgical team
options.B: Reviewing the medication administration record for recent antibiotic changes
options.C: Attributing the symptoms solely to the primary illness without checking for treatment complications
options.D: Checking the surgical incision site for signs of localized redness or drainage

explanation: Spot on! Assuming every new symptom is just the original disease can blind us to hospital infections, drug reactions, or other unexpected complications. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h4)

question: What does a low height-for-age measurement mainly tell us about a young child?

options.A: Chronic undernutrition or stunting
options.B: Immediate short-term weight loss
options.C: Excessive daily caloric intake
options.D: Acute rapid dehydration

explanation: Height-for-age looks at the long picture. If it's low, it usually points to stunting caused by long-term poor nutrition or repeated illnesses over time. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h5)

question: What is a primary benefit of addressing workplace conflicts early in a clinical setting?

options.A: It prevents small disagreements from turning into a toxic atmosphere
options.B: It removes the need for shift handovers and team meetings
options.C: It stops doctors from ever questioning nursing care plans
options.D: It guarantees that nurses receive an immediate salary increase

explanation: Correct! Addressing issues early keeps the ward vibe positive and ensures patient safety stays front and center. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h7)

question: Why is the transformation zone easily prone to irritation?

options.A: It has a very thick layer of hard skin cells that easily trap heat.
options.B: It experiences constant muscular contractions during the menstrual period.
options.C: It features active cell transitions that make it vulnerable to external factors.
options.D: It lacks any protective mucus layer to shield it from normal bacteria.

explanation: Correct! Because cells are actively changing and meeting right there, this zone is extra sensitive to infections and friction. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h2)

question: Why is teaching the family so important before sending a neuro client home?

options.A: Clients with brain injuries never regain their memory or thinking skills
options.B: Family members are legally required to pass a written nursing exam
options.C: Caregivers need to recognize warning signs of complications and manage daily care
options.D: Home health nurses are not allowed to visit clients after discharge

explanation: Since family members will be doing the heavy lifting at home, they need to know what red flags mean it's time to rush back to the hospital. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h8)

question: Why should a nurse apply gentle pressure to the nasolacrimal duct after giving eye drops?

options.A: To help spread the liquid evenly across the eyeball surface
options.B: To stop the patient from blinking too rapidly
options.C: To seal the eyelids shut until the medication dries completely
options.D: To keep the medication from draining into the nasal passage and causing systemic effects

explanation: Blocking the tear duct stops the medicine from entering the nose and bloodstream, keeping its action localized to the eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is obstetric fistula?

options.A: The premature closing of the birth canal due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: A sudden infection of the outer reproductive organs during early pregnancy
options.C: An abnormal opening between the vagina and bladder or rectum caused by prolonged labor
options.D: A complete failure of the ovaries to release eggs during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Well done! When labor is blocked in a narrow pelvis, the crushed tissue dies, leaving a hole (fistula) that causes leaking of urine or stool. It's a devastating condition we work hard to prevent. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h2)

question: Why is a primary health care nurse in a great position to monitor community diseases?

options.A: They possess the authority to declare national state emergencies
options.B: They interact directly with local patients and see early signs of illness
options.C: They work exclusively inside high-tech research laboratories abroad
options.D: They are responsible for importing vaccines from international suppliers

explanation: Because community nurses talk to patients every single day, they are usually the very first to notice when something unusual is going on. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h6)

question: Why can synergistic drug combinations sometimes lead to unexpected toxicity?

options.A: The patient's immune system attacks the combination as a foreign invader
options.B: The pills dissolve too quickly before entering the bloodstream
options.C: The drugs automatically turn into poisonous substances in the stomach
options.D: The enhanced potency applies to adverse reactions as well as therapeutic effects

explanation: Synergy is a double-edged sword! It boosts the good healing effects, but it can also accidentally ramp up nasty side effects. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h6)

question: A nurse and a doctor argue because both want to decide the exact time to discharge a patient. What is the root cause here?

options.A: An absolute surplus of transport vehicles
options.B: Identical professional backgrounds
options.C: Role ambiguity and power imbalance
options.D: A complete lack of patient admission records

explanation: When two professionals clash over who has the final say, it usually means their job boundaries overlap and power is being contested. [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why do brain cells start swelling up (edema) when they run out of energy during a stroke?

options.A: The skull instantly expands to pull excess fluid out of the bloodstream.
options.B: The sodium-potassium pump stops working, allowing water and sodium to rush inside.
options.C: Damaged neurons start producing excess amounts of fatty storage oils.
options.D: Red blood cells leak out of intact capillaries and flood the ventricles.

explanation: Without energy (ATP), tiny cellular pumps fail. Sodium and water rush into the cell, making it swell up like a balloon. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T19#GNS222_U3_T19_h4)

question: Which part of the digestive tract does ulcerative colitis mainly affect?

options.A: The entire small intestine
options.B: The colon and rectum
options.C: The mouth and esophagus
options.D: The stomach and duodenum

explanation: Ulcerative colitis stays in the large intestine. It starts down in the rectum and can spread upward in a steady, continuous line. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h3)

question: A pregnant woman comes to the clinic for a routine checkup. What should the midwife focus on first?

options.A: Scheduling her for an immediate cesarean section
options.B: Referring her directly to a pediatric specialist
options.C: Screening for pregnancy complications like high blood pressure
options.D: Admitting her for long-term bed rest in the ward

explanation: Great thinking! Routine antenatal visits are all about catching little issues early—like checking blood pressure to prevent complications before they start. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which common health condition is a major cause of sudden breathlessness in Nigerian hospital wards?

options.A: Severe anaemia
options.B: Hemophilia A
options.C: Polycythaemia vera
options.D: Thrombocytopenia

explanation: Great job! Severe anaemia—often linked to malaria or poor nutrition—means fewer red blood cells to carry oxygen, making the patient breathe faster to compensate. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge that stops nurses from sharing their research?

options.A: An overabundance of free time during shifts
options.B: Lack of funding for open-access publication fees
options.C: Hospitals forcing all nurses to publish weekly papers
options.D: Too many journals competing to publish clinical studies

explanation: Well done! Publishing fees can be quite expensive, which unfortunately blocks many nurses from getting their work out in open-access journals. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h6)

question: How full can a sharps box get before you must close and replace it?

options.A: One-quarter full
options.B: Completely packed to the top rim
options.C: Whenever it starts smelling bad
options.D: Three-quarters full

explanation: Safety first! Always seal and replace sharps containers when they are three-quarters full so needles don't poke out and accidentally injure someone. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is a common myth about teaching young people about sexual health?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for primary healthcare clinics
options.B: It is illegal under all international human rights laws
options.C: It causes severe physical side effects in teenagers
options.D: It encourages promiscuity and early sexual activity

explanation: Exactly! Many people wrongly fear that talking about sex encourages it, but studies show education actually helps youth make safer choices and wait longer. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h4)

question: During a quick neuro check, which finding is usually the most urgent warning sign of a worsening brain condition?

options.A: A mild drop in the patient's daily appetite
options.B: A temporary change in skin color tone
options.C: A slight increase in overall body temperature
options.D: A sudden drop in the motor response score

explanation: When a patient's movement or motor response suddenly drops, it is often a major red flag for brain swelling or injury. Stay alert! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended way for a nurse administrator to manage goal conflicts?

options.A: Enforcing clear hospital policies while supporting staff
options.B: Implementing fair and transparent shift scheduling
options.C: Using open communication and active listening
options.D: Firing all staff members immediately without discussion

explanation: Harsh, instant firing destroys team morale! Good leaders solve conflicts by talking things through, listening, and being fair. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient shows signs of a severe adverse drug reaction?

options.A: Wait until the doctor finishes the ward round
options.B: Ask the patient to sign a refusal of treatment form
options.C: Increase the fluid intake to dilute the drug
options.D: Discontinue the offending medication right away

explanation: Stop the drug first! Cutting off the source is your priority before doing anything else to help. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the true foundation of evidence-based practice in nursing?

options.A: Following the personal opinions of senior administrative staff
options.B: Using the cheapest medical supplies available on the market
options.C: Strict adherence to traditional hospital routines
options.D: Combining best research evidence with clinical expertise and patient values

explanation: You've got it! Evidence-based practice is a sweet spot: it blends what science proves works, your clinical skills as a nurse, and what the patient actually wants. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why is a patient usually asked to lie flat after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: To help prevent a low-pressure spinal headache
options.B: To speed up the absorption of the local anesthetic
options.C: To keep the blood pressure from dropping too fast
options.D: To prevent the collection tubes from falling over

explanation: Correct! Lying flat reduces pull on the meninges where the needle went in, lowering the chance of a terrible headache. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the main heart and philosophy behind home health nursing?

options.A: Promoting patient empowerment and self-care within their environment
options.B: Isolating the patient from family members to prevent infection
options.C: Transferring all decision-making power entirely to the physician
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital routines inside private residences

explanation: Well done! It's all about helping patients and their families feel confident to manage their own health right where they live. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T1#GNS324_U1_T1_h2)

question: A toddler in a home suffers skin burns from a pot of hot soup on the floor. What kind of accident is this?

options.A: An occupational accident
options.B: A domestic accident
options.C: A road traffic accident
options.D: An industrial accident

explanation: Mishaps like burns, cuts, and falls that happen right inside or around the home environment are called domestic accidents. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h2)

question: What communication style should a nurse use when counseling a caregiver who defaulted on vaccines?

options.A: Total silence while the caregiver reads a pamphlet
options.B: Rapid medical terminology to prove professional status
options.C: Strict lecturing to show authority and clinical power
options.D: Respectful listening and clear, non-judgmental explanations

explanation: Caregivers respond better to patience and empathy than to strict scolding, which often makes them avoid the clinic permanently. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h5)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in home care?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Restricting all visitors permanently
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns all day
options.D: Spraying rooms with strong perfumes

explanation: Good old-fashioned handwashing is your best defense! It removes germs and stops them from passing between you and your patients. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h6)

question: During which step of mobilisation do community members and nurses figure out what resources and tasks are needed?

options.A: Immediate closure
options.B: Final evaluation
options.C: Strict policing
options.D: Action planning

explanation: Action planning is where the community maps out tasks, responsibilities, and timelines using local resources. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is a complete large bowel blockage considered a serious medical emergency?

options.A: High pressure can cause the bowel wall to rupture and spill contents
options.B: It immediately stops the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: It stops the liver from filtering toxins from the blood
options.D: It always causes permanent brain damage within two hours

explanation: Spot on! As gas and stool pile up behind the blockage, pressure builds, cutting off blood flow and risking a dangerous rupture (perforation). [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why is spotting a specific 'toxidrome' (group of symptoms) so helpful in emergency care?

options.A: It proves legal liability for workplace safety violations
options.B: It stops the chemical from absorbing through unbroken skin
options.C: It guides rapid clinical management before lab tests confirm the toxin
options.D: It eliminates the need to decontaminate the patient's clothing

explanation: Lab tests take time! Spotting a familiar pattern of symptoms lets you start life-saving antidotes and care right away. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T5#GNS215_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which severe obstetric complication is frequently linked to early childbearing before the pelvis is fully developed?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Obstetric fistula
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Prolonged and obstructed labor in an immature pelvis creates abnormal holes between the birth canal and bladder or rectum, leading to continuous leakage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h3)

question: Why should you warn patients about mild side effects before they start a new drug?

options.A: To eliminate all possibility of severe allergic reactions developing later
options.B: To guarantee that the pharmacy receives full payment for the prescription
options.C: To prevent them from stopping the medication in panic when side effects occur
options.D: To ensure the patient stops taking the medication at the first sign of discomfort

explanation: A forewarned patient stays calm when mild side effects pop up and sticks to their treatment plan. Great patient education! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why is maintaining good musculoskeletal health so important for a patient?

options.A: It prevents all forms of infectious diseases
options.B: It completely stops the natural aging process
options.C: It preserves daily mobility and personal independence
options.D: It lowers the patient's blood pressure levels

explanation: Healthy bones, joints, and muscles allow a person to move freely and care for themselves without relying on others. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h1)

question: Why is it dangerous to give rescue breaths too fast or with too much force?

options.A: It can force air into the stomach and lead to vomiting
options.B: It immediately collapses both lungs due to high pressure
options.C: It causes the patient's heart rate to drop dangerously low
options.D: It forces blood backward into the jugular veins

explanation: Easy does it with breaths! Blowing too hard opens up the stomach instead of the lungs, which can cause the patient to vomit and complicate things. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h5)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient receiving an infusion of oxytocin to stimulate labor contractions. Which risk requires the nurse to monitor this patient most closely?

options.A: Severe fetal distress from hyperstimulation
options.B: Sudden vision loss and chronic migraines
options.C: Total paralysis of the lower extremities
options.D: Sudden development of adult asthma

explanation: Oxytocin is a high-alert drug that causes uterine contractions; too much medicine can cause contractions that are too strong or frequent, cutting off oxygen to the baby. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why do older adults often need fewer total calories but still require plenty of vitamins and minerals?

options.A: They have a slower metabolism, but still need nutrients to protect bones and muscles
options.B: Their digestive systems completely stop absorbing all forms of dietary fat
options.C: Older adults naturally stop growing taller, so their cells no longer need any energy
options.D: They require fewer nutrients because their bodies are fully mature

explanation: As people age, their bodies burn less energy overall, but they still need a good mix of vitamins and minerals to keep bones strong and prevent muscle loss. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h5)

question: Why are pregnant women told to avoid unpasteurized dairy and deli meats?

options.A: These foods always cause immediate skin rashes
options.B: They are at high risk for dangerous Listeria infections
options.C: These items contain artificial food colors
options.D: Pregnant women cannot digest animal protein

explanation: You got it! Listeria is sneaky and can cross the placenta, causing serious harm to a pregnancy. That's why we always educate expectant mothers to steer clear! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T010#GNS227_U3_T010_h4)

question: What is the main cause of drug resistance in patients taking HIV treatment?

options.A: Inconsistent medication adherence allowing viral replication during low drug levels
options.B: Eating heavy fatty meals right before taking the evening dose
options.C: Swallowing pills with cold water instead of warm water
options.D: Storing medication bottles in brightly lit hospital rooms

explanation: Spot on! Missing doses leaves gaps where drug levels drop, giving the virus room to multiply and mutate against the medication. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h6)

question: What is the main focus of a National Drug Policy compared to a general health policy?

options.A: Pharmaceuticals and medicine supply chains
options.B: Medical doctor and nurse salary structures
options.C: Hospital building construction and maintenance
options.D: Global health donor funding negotiations

explanation: Think of it this way: while a general health policy looks at everything in healthcare, a National Drug Policy zooms in specifically on medicines—making sure they are produced, distributed, and used safely! [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of the National Programme on Immunization?

options.A: Treating chronic non-communicable illnesses in adults
options.B: Supplying essential nutrition supplements to pregnant women
options.C: Protecting populations from vaccine-preventable diseases
options.D: Providing free surgical care for newborn congenital defects

explanation: The NPI focuses specifically on preventing infectious diseases through safe and effective vaccination schedules. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: Which of these is classified as 'sharps' waste?

options.A: Hypodermic needles and scalpel blades
options.B: Disposable paper bed sheets
options.C: Cotton wool balls and surgical gauze
options.D: Plastic IV fluid bags and tubing

explanation: Easy and clear! Needles and blades have sharp edges that can puncture skin, so they need special handling. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is gender discrimination in community health primarily based on?

options.A: Family income level and education
options.B: Geographical location of residence
options.C: Biological sex or gender identity
options.D: Professional occupation and status

explanation: Gender discrimination is specifically rooted in bias against an individual's biological sex or how they identify in terms of gender. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h1)

question: What hemoglobin level tells us a woman has anaemia during labor?

options.A: Below 14.5 g/dL
options.B: Below 11.0 g/dL
options.C: Below 12.5 g/dL
options.D: Below 10.0 g/dL

explanation: Great to know! The WHO sets 11.0 g/dL as the cutoff for pregnant and laboring women. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h1)

question: Which chemical messengers in the brain play a major role in mood and depression?

options.A: Serotonin and norepinephrine
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Sodium and potassium

explanation: Well done! Serotonin and norepinephrine are key neurotransmitters that help regulate our mood. An imbalance here is a big part of why depression happens. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h3)

question: A patient loves sweets and is struggling to cut them out completely. What is a smart, gradual first goal?

options.A: Buying expensive sugar-free substitutes from abroad
options.B: Stopping all sugar consumption immediately today
options.C: Replacing sugary snacks with fruit on alternate days
options.D: Ignoring the sweet intake until the next hospital visit

explanation: You're thinking like a pro nurse! Small, baby steps are way easier for patients to stick with than sudden, impossible restrictions. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h5)

question: How does community-based rehabilitation help fight against social stigma?

options.A: By involving local leaders and educating the public about disabilities
options.B: By forcing communities to build expensive private hospitals
options.C: By restricting public gatherings for people with chronic illnesses
options.D: By hiding individuals with disabilities away from public view

explanation: Education clears up misunderstandings. When local communities learn together, they start seeing the person first, not the disability. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h4)

question: How should a nurse apply a prescribed cream onto a patient's forearm?
